summary: FireSight is a satellite fire intelligence platform that makes MODIS and VIIRS hotspot observations easier to explore and compare. It preserves original satellite records and harmonizes detected activity into a common spatial grid and daily time framework. Through interactive maps, a harmonized burning activity calendar, sensor comparison, regional analysis and research exports, FireSight helps researchers and environmental organisations better understand satellite-observed fire activity.
details:
FireSight addresses the challenge of comparing fire hotspot observations from different satellite instruments, particularly MODIS and VIIRS.

These satellites observe fire activity using different characteristics, detection capabilities and observation schedules. Consequently, their hotspot records cannot simply be combined by adding their detection counts.

FireSight collects and preserves original satellite observations from NASA FIRMS. It organises observations into a common spatial grid and daily time framework using its HAI-OCCUPANCY harmonization approach. The system calculates daily spatial activity coverage by combining occupied grid cells while avoiding duplicate counting of overlapping cells.

The platform provides an interactive fire map, harmonized burning activity calendar, sensor comparison, regional analysis, data validation, uncertainty information and research exports.

FireSight is designed to support environmental researchers, government agencies, universities, conservation organisations and geospatial analysts.

The platform does not claim to calculate unique fire incidents or burned area, and its harmonization approach does not represent a calibrated conversion between MODIS and VIIRS measurements.
